newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq welcomes U.N. statement on plane.
newsitem.headline: Iraq welcomes U.N. statement on plane.

text.p: Iraq on Thursday welcomed a U.N. Security Council statement which stopped short of calling a recent Iraqi pilgrim flight to Saudi Arabia a violation of Gulf War sanctions.
Baghdad newspapers, which carried the statement on their front pages, also issued remarks by a foreign ministry source reiterating Iraq's right to send civilian planes beyond its borders.

"The source lauded the legal and understanding attitude shown by a number of members of the Security Council during deliberations ... during which they expressed their obvious realisation that the American stand vis-a-vis this subject is illegal and unfair," the source said.

The Security Council, in a setback for the United States, issued a mild statement on Wednesday that refrained from calling the flight a breach of the sanctions imposed after Iraq's August 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
The statement, the result of several days of negotiations, said Iraq proceeded with the flight "without specific consultation" with the council's Iraqi sanctions committee.
The source said Iraq did not need to ask for permission to fly its civilian planes since it deemed such an undertaking as part of its natural right.
He said the issuing of the statement by the council did not mean that Iraq had no right in future to use its planes for international flights.
Iraqi leaders said in a meeting chaired by President Saddam Hussein on Saturday the United Nations embargo on Iraq did not prevent it from using its civilian aircratf outside the country.
